The core innovation of flexBART lies in replacing traditional one-hot encoding with a multi-level split prior that allows direct partitioning of categorical variables without combinatorial explosion. This addresses the fundamental limitation where one-hot encoding restricts the number of reachable partitions to 2^K - K instead of the theoretically possible K-th Bell number. The method leverages Bayesian backfitting via Gibbs sampling to iteratively update leaf parameters, ensuring convergence while maintaining interpretability. In the context of GSI, this enables robust conformal prediction on categorical sports data such as player identities and game states. For GSE, it supports dynamic state transitions by allowing adaptive grouping of similar categories based on observed outcomes rather than fixed encodings. The network extension further enhances applicability to relational data like team hierarchies or geographic clusters.
